prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create an accurate, friendly educational infographic about fitting clock errors within a permitted interval. Landscape 3:2, pure warm-white background, soft watercolor accents and thin colored-pencil outlines, large crisp navy English text. Main title: 'Every error must fit inside the limits'. Two stacked comparison panels with IDENTICAL horizontal error scales and spacing. Each scale has exactly labeled ticks at −2, −1, 0, +1, +2, and its label is 'Remaining error (min)'. Shade ONLY the interval from −1 to +1 pale teal on both panels, including its boundaries; caption for shared band: 'Allowed interval: −1 to +1 min'. TOP panel title: 'q = 0 min'. Exactly four data dots: one gray dot at −2, two separate blue dots vertically stacked at −1, one blue dot at 0. Place dots above the ticks with vertical alignment guides so their x-values are unambiguous. Gray −2 dot lies outside the band. Top panel verdict: 'Reject: one error is outside'. BOTTOM panel title: 'q = 1 min'. Exactly four blue data dots: one at −1, two separate blue dots vertically stacked at 0, one at +1. All are inside or ON the teal band boundaries. Bottom panel verdict: 'Accept: all four errors fit'. The repeated observations must be visible as two distinct vertically stacked dots, never merged into one. Both scales share exactly the same range, same band and same zero position. A tiny blue adjustment dial at the left can echo the classroom clock setting, but must not intrude on the scales. No stars, optimization algorithm, extra numeric values, third panel, extra dots, distorted axis spacings, equations, labels or watermark. All text readable at 800 px display width.
